title: Validation tests claim 'fires nothing' but never assert the no-fire property
evidence:
+/// Save with an empty name shows the inline error, fires nothing.
+  let #(updated, eff) = client.update(m, msg.UserSavedRefcheckEdit("rc-1"))
+  case updated.refcheck_edit {
+    option.Some(edit) ->
+      edit.error |> should.equal(option.Some(copy.refcheck_edit_need_name))
+    option.None -> should.fail()
+  }
+/// Save with no reachable channel shows the channel error, fires nothing.
+  case updated.refcheck_edit {
+    option.Some(edit) ->
+      edit.error |> should.equal(option.Some(copy.refcheck_edit_need_channel))
detail: Both tests assert only the inline error. A regression that fires the endpoint on validation failure (dropping effect.none()) passes them; 'fires nothing' is unpinned. The unused `eff` binding shows no-fire was meant to be checked.
recommended_fix: Assert refcheck_action_inflight does not contain the call_id (and/or the edit's saving stays False) in both tests, or drop the 'fires nothing' claim.

evidence:

+  let #(updated, eff) =

detail: gleam emits 'This variable is never used' for each (verified by compiling). Every sibling test in the same diff uses `_eff`; these four deviate and add warning noise.
recommended_fix: Rename the bindings to `_eff` in the four tests.

title: Fieldless record update `model.Model(..model.initial())` — a no-op that emits a compiler warning
detail: Spread with no field changes equals model.initial(); gleam warns 'This record update doesn't change any fields' (verified by compiling). Suggests an intended field override was forgotten.
recommended_fix: Use `let m = model.initial()` (or add the intended field overrides).

title: New import line `import model.{type RefcheckConfirm, type RefcheckEdit}` is entirely unused
detail: Both imported types are never referenced — tests use the qualified `model.RefcheckConfirm`/`model.RefcheckEdit` forms. gleam warns 'This imported type is never used' for both (verified by compiling).

title: objected_row_substitute_surface_test re-declares the hooks record the new base_hooks() helper exists to provide, shadowing it
evidence:
+fn base_hooks() -> reference_call.ReferenceCallHooks {
+    can_record_manual: False,
+    can_substitute_referee: False,
+    can_retry: False,
+    can_take_over: False,
+  )
+  let base_hooks =
+    reference_call.ReferenceCallHooks(
+      can_record_manual: False,
+      can_substitute_referee: False,
+      can_retry: False,
+      can_take_over: False,
+    )
detail: The local `base_hooks` value duplicates the module-level `base_hooks()` function added in this same diff and shadows its name; two sources of truth for the same default that can diverge.
recommended_fix: Use the module helper: `hooks: reference_call.ReferenceCallHooks(..base_hooks(), can_substitute_referee: True)`.
